entities.evidence: Genesis 4:19 names Adah as one of Lamech’s wives. Here she bears Jabal.
Jabal is the son Adah bears here. The verse calls him the father of those who live in tents and keep livestock.

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular verb agrees with its subject עָדָה (Adah). The direct-object marker אֶת introduces יָבָל (Jabal), the child she bore.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add a personal-name article linked to the root עדה.
draft.definition: A Hebrew personal name borne here by Jabal’s mother.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:19 explicitly gives her name as עָדָה. Genesis 4:20 uses that name again when she gives birth to Jabal.

analysis.evidence: In וַתֵּלֶד עָדָה אֶת יָבָל, the feminine singular verb וַתֵּלֶד agrees with its subject עָדָה, and אֶת marks Jabal as the child she bore. Genesis 4:19 names Adah as one of Lamech’s wives.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular proper noun, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Adah, Lamech’s wife and Jabal’s mother

analysis.evidence: In וַתֵּלֶד עָדָה אֶת יָבָל, עָדָה is the subject of וַתֵּלֶד (“bore”), and אֶת marks the personal name יָבָל as its definite direct object (“Adah bore Jabal”).
analysis.morphology: Unsuffixed direct-object particle with no prefix.

analysis.evidence: In וַתֵּלֶד עָדָה אֶת יָבָל, אֶת marks Jabal as the child Adah bore. The following הוּא refers back to him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, direct object of וַתֵּלֶד, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to יָבָל (Jabal) and serves as the subject of הָיָה in הוּא הָיָה אֲבִי, “he was the father of.”
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to Jabal. הָיָה connects that subject to the predicate אֲבִי, identifying Jabal as the father of those who live in tents and keep livestock.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: אֲבִי introduces יֹשֵׁב אֹהֶל וּמִקְנֶה, a collective description of tent-dwelling herders. The verse calls Jabal their father in the sense that he originated their way of life.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: יֹשֵׁב אֹהֶל means “tent dweller.” The singular participle names the class of people for whom Jabal is called אָבִי, “the father of.” It describes their customary way of living.
analysis.gloss: one who lives in a tent
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, used substantivally.
analysis.sense: to dwell habitually in a place

analysis.evidence: In יֹשֵׁב אֹהֶל, “one who dwells in a tent,” אֹהֶל names the shelter in which the person lives. The accompanying mention of livestock fits this pastoral setting.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse calls Jabal the father of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock. The pairing of אֹהֶל ‘tent’ with מִקְנֶה evokes pastoral life. ‘Keep’ is understood from the context.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.
